t.1.118.1: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Vidura, have all the funeral rites of Pāṇḍu, that lion among kings, performed in royal fashion, and those of Mādrī too, with special care.
t.1.118.2: On behalf of Pāṇḍu and Mādrī, give away cattle, garments, jewels and riches of many kinds, to whoever desires them and as much as they desire.
t.1.118.4: The sinless Pāṇḍu is not to be mourned; that lord of men is to be praised, he to whom were born five heroic sons equal to the sons of the gods.
t.1.118.5: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Saying "So be it" to him, O Bhārata, Vidura, together with Bhīṣma, had the funeral rites of Pāṇḍu performed in a well-secluded place.
t.1.118.3: And arrange things so that Kuntī may pay due honor to Mādrī, and so that neither the wind nor the sun may look upon her, well covered as she is.
t.1.118.6: Then the royal priests swiftly brought forth from the city the blazing fires of Pāṇḍu, honored with oblations of clarified butter.
t.1.118.7: Then, having covered it all over with cloth, they adorned him and the litter with seasonal flowers and fragrances and with various excellent garlands.
t.1.118.8: The ministers, the kinsmen, and the friends drew near to that bier, thus adorned with garlands and with garments of great value.
t.1.118.10: Then they adorned it with a white parasol and a yak-tail fan, and with the sounds of all kinds of musical instruments.
t.1.118.9: They carried him, that lion among men, well shrouded, together with Mādrī, on a splendid, richly adorned bier borne by men.
t.1.118.11: Taking up many jewels as well, the men there gave them away by the hundreds to those who desired them, as the funeral rite for Pāṇḍu.
t.1.118.12: Then for the sake of the Kaurava they brought shining umbrellas, white and large, and beautiful garments.
t.1.118.14: Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas and Śūdras by the thousands, weeping and burning with grief, followed the lord of men.
t.1.118.13: The sacrificial fires, fed with oblations by white-robed priests, went on ahead of him, blazing and finely adorned.
t.1.118.15: Having abandoned us and plunged us into everlasting sorrow, having made us protectorless, where will this king of men, our supreme protector, go?
t.1.118.16: All the Pāṇḍavas, wailing aloud, and Bhīṣma and Vidura as well, at a delightful spot in the forest, on the level and auspicious bank of the Gaṅgā…
t.1.118.18: Then they quickly sprinkled with water from vessels made of gold that body of his, perfumed with every fragrance, anointed with pure kālīyaka sandal, and scented with the finest bathing preparations.
t.1.118.17: Then the truthful men had that palanquin set down, the palanquin of Pāṇḍu, lion among men and doer of tireless deeds, together with his wife.
t.1.118.20: Then they clothed him in white garments made in their own land; and, covered with those garments, that bull among men, that tiger among men, accustomed to costly beds, shone as though he were still alive.
t.1.118.19: They anointed him with the finest white sandalwood mixed with black aloewood, and likewise with the essence of tuṅga.
t.1.118.21: The king, together with Mādrī, sprinkled with ghee and finely adorned, was permitted by the officiating priests, who were well versed in the rites for the dead.
t.1.118.24: Seeing her fallen and stricken with grief, all the people of the city and the countryside, filled with compassion out of devotion to the king, wept aloud.
t.1.118.22: They had the bodies burned with fragrant sandalwood mixed with tuṅga and padmaka, and with many other perfumes of various kinds in abundance.
t.1.118.23: Then, seeing the two bodies of those two, Kausalyā was overcome by delusion and, crying "Alas, alas, my son!", suddenly fell to the ground.
t.1.118.25: As if exhausted, all beings cried out with a sound of anguish, together with humans, even those born in the wombs of animals.
t.1.118.26: Likewise Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, and the greatly wise Vidura, and all the Kauravas too, deeply grief-stricken, cried out loudly.
t.1.118.27: Then Bhīṣma, Vidura, and the king together with his kinsmen, and all the women of the Kurus, offered the water libation for him.
t.1.118.28: Taking with them the Pāṇḍavas, who had offered the water libations and were worn down by grief, all the subjects, O king, grieving, gathered around them.
t.1.118.29: Just as the Pāṇḍavas slept on the ground together with their kinsmen, so too, O king, did the townspeople, the brāhmaṇas and the rest, lie down upon the ground.
t.1.118.30: Together with the Pāṇḍavas, that city, down to its very children, remained joyless, ill at ease and as if cheerless for twelve nights.
